name: Southern Ohio Data Center Campus
notes: Proposed on the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site in Pike County; paired with a dedicated 9.2 GW on-site natural gas power plant, one of the largest gas-fired facilities ever proposed. Financed by SoftBank.

name: Meta Richland Parish Campus
notes: 4-million-sq-ft campus that could scale to 5 GW eventually. Entergy Louisiana is building three combined-cycle gas turbines (2,260 MW combined) at Holly Ridge and Waterford to serve the load, alongside grid interconnection.

name: Stargate Abilene
notes: Flagship Stargate site on the Lancium Clean Campus. Operates on a natural gas microgrid (permitted for 360 MW of on-site turbines) independent of the Oncor grid to bypass interconnection queue delays; expanding toward 1.2 GW.

name: xAI Colossus
notes: South Memphis supercomputer campus. Combines grid supply with ~35 on-site natural gas turbines (~420-500 MW) and Tesla Megapack battery storage; turbine count has drawn scrutiny for exceeding permitted limits.

name: AWS Rainier (New Carlisle)
notes: 1,200-acre campus in St. Joseph County designed for 2.2 GW across ~30 buildings; first phase opened October 2025. Grid-supplied via Indiana utilities.

name: Microsoft Fairwater (Mount Pleasant)
notes: Flagship AI data center campus in Racine County. Phase 1 (400 MW) completed June 2026; campus projected to reach 3.3 GW peak electrical load by late 2027. Grid-supplied.

name: Meta Prometheus (New Albany)
notes: Billed as the world's first gigawatt-capable data center. Backed by ~400 MW of on-site private natural gas generation (Socrates South) plus nuclear power agreements with TerraPower, Oklo, and Vistra.

name: AWS Madison County Mega Site (Canton)
notes: ~1 GW data center complex in Canton, part of a $25B Amazon investment across Mississippi. Backed by 1.3 GW of new solar/wind commitments with Entergy plus >700 diesel generators for backup.

name: Google Council Bluffs
notes: One of Google's oldest and largest U.S. campuses, opened 2007, on the wind-heavy MidAmerican Energy grid.

name: Meta Prineville
notes: One of Meta's first wholly-owned U.S. data center campuses; multiple buildings built to LEED Gold standard with PUE ~1.06. Grid-supplied.

name: Amazon / Energy Northwest SMR Campus
developer: Amazon Web Services / X-energy / Energy Northwest
notes: Planned deployment of 12 X-energy Xe-100 small modular nuclear reactors (80 MWe each) near the Columbia Generating Station in Richland, targeting carbon-free power for AWS data centers.
